title: Before You Continue: Evaluating Time-Sensitive Safety Awareness in Conversational Assistants
abstract: arXiv:2611.06839v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) assistants increasingly help users with everyday activities that involve time-dependent constraints. However, users may not mention these constraints in later requests, requiring assistants to recognize and adjust their advice accordingly. To evaluate such capability, we introduce TASC (Temporal Action Safety in Conversation), a benchmark that evaluates whether LLMs apply time-dependent constraints when responding to conversational requests. TASC consists of 3,418 inputs derived from 128 templates, along with a separate set of 33 scenarios designed to compare models' ability to calculate elapsed time with their ability to apply that information. Across 13 models, assistants account for time-dependent constraints in only 30.5% of cases where the proposed action violates a rule, while rarely warning users unnecessarily. translated_title: 在你继续之前：评估对话助手中的时间敏感安全意识
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）助手日益帮助用户处理涉及时间相关约束的日常活动。然而，用户在后续请求中可能不会提及这些约束，这就要求助手能够识别这些约束并相应调整其建议。为评估这种能力，我们提出了TASC（Temporal Action Safety in Conversation，对话中的时间性动作安全）基准，用于评估LLM在回应对话请求时是否考虑时间相关约束。TASC包含由128个模板生成的3,418个输入，以及一个单独的包含33个场景的集合，旨在比较模型计算经过时间的能力与其应用该信息的能力。在对13个模型的测试中，助手在所提议动作违反规则的案例中仅有30.5%考虑了时间相关约束，同时很少发出不必要的警告。更重要的是，模型在62.1%的案例中尽管正确计算了……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出TASC基准评估LLM助手是否在对话中考虑时间相关约束，发现13个模型在动作违反规则的案例中仅有30.5%考虑了时间约束，且在62.1%的案例中尽管能正确计算时间信息却未能加以应用。
en_tdlr: Introduces TASC, a benchmark evaluating whether LLM assistants apply time-dependent constraints in conversations, revealing that across 13 models, assistants consider such constraints in only 30.5% of rule-violating cases and fail to apply correctly calculated time information in 62.1% of cases.
